item.title: Tesoro argentino coloca unos 4.367,4 mln dlr en licitación de títulos
item.description: Argentina otorgó títulos del Tesoro por un valor efectivo de 6,61 billones de pesos (unos 4.367,4 millones de dólares) en una licitación interna de diferentes instrumentos para refinanciar vencimientos de corto plazo, informó el miércoles la Secretaría de Finanzas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Argentina otorgó títulos del Tesoro por un valor efectivo de 6,61 billones de pesos (unos 4.367,4 millones de dólares) en una licitación interna de diferentes instrumentos para refinanciar vencimientos de corto plazo, informó el miércoles la Secretaría de Finanzas. La licitación, por la que se recibió un total de ofertas por 9,49 billones de pesos, abarcó una renovación ('rollover') del 136,14% de los vencimientos previstos. El Tesoro buscó reemplazar originalmente unos 4,9 billones de pesos en vencimientos de deuda interna. El menú ofertado consistió en una letra 'Lecap' (S29E7), el bono 'Bontam' (TMG28), el título dual 'CER/Tamar' (TXMD9) y el dual 'FX/Tamar' (TMVE8). (1 dólar = 1.513,5 pesos )

item.title: US Supreme Court again backs Republicans in clash over political ad rates
item.description: The US Supreme Court again sided with Republicans on Wednesday in the latest clash over a new Federal Communications Commission policy that gives party committees access to discounted TV and radio advertising rates long available to political candidates.
item.dc:creator: John Kruzel
item.content:encoded: The US Supreme Court again sided with Republicans on Wednesday in the latest clash over a new Federal Communications Commission policy that gives party committees access to discounted TV and radio advertising rates long available to political candidates. The court agreed to let the FCC, which is chaired by Trump ally Brendan Carr, avoid a judicially imposed deadline that would have forced the agency to rule on a Democratic challenge to the policy before the November 3 midterm elections. The FCC joined two Republican committees in filing a request to the Supreme Court to lift the lower court's deadline. The court has a 6-3 conservative majority. Liberal Justices Sonia Sotomayor and Ketanji Brown Jackson indicated they would have denied the request. The FCC, which currently has a 2-1 Republican majority, modified its so-called "lowest unit charge" rule in March in a move seen as a boost to President Donald Trump 's fellow Republicans. The president's party is seeking to retain control of Congress in the November 3 midterms. "We are pleased the Supreme Court has granted the FCC's stay request. The court's decision is right on the law and avoids the specter of upending the rules for political ads right in the middle of an ongoing election," an FCC spokesperson said. Chief Justice John Roberts had previously lifted the October 9 deadline that was given to the FCC by the Richmond-based 4th US Circuit Court of Appeals. The 4th Circuit has accused the FCC of repeated "delay tactics" in the case, and emphasized the need for an urgent ruling in the Democratic challenge given the looming election. The Supreme Court's latest action marks the second time in recent weeks that it has addressed the FCC's policy, as major Republican committees head toward the midterms with a cash advantage over their Democratic counterparts. In September, the court [USN:S0N41Y02H TEXT:"granted"] a request by the national Republican committees that support the party's candidates in Senate and House of Representatives races to revive the policy after the 4th Circuit blocked it. The justices in an 8-1 ruling said that the Democratic candidates must wait for the FCC to rule before filing a challenge in court. The FCC policy at issue requires broadcasters to charge discounted rates for airing certain political advertisements within 60 days of a general election, a window that opened this year on September 4. A group of Democratic candidates including Senator Jon Ossoff of Georgia in April challenged the policy through in-house proceedings at the FCC. When the agency took no action, the Democrats successfully challenged the policy in the 4th Circuit, a ruling that was later halted by the Supreme Court. The 4th Circuit on October 7 ordered the FCC to issue a prompt ruling on the Democratic in-house challenge, more than five months after it was filed. In its 2-1 ruling, the 4th Circuit said its "willingness to tolerate the FCC's delay tactics is at an end." 'TRENCH WARFARE' The Republican committees in their Supreme Court filing accused the 4th Circuit of having "short-circuited" the FCC's review process. The Democratic candidates, for their part, accused the FCC in court papers of engaging in "blatant procedural trench warfare to stave off judicial review of an unlawful agency directive until it is too late to matter." The FCC policy gained greater significance after the Supreme Court in June [USN:L1N4310Y4 TEXT:"struck down"] federal restrictions on spending coordinated between parties and their candidates, siding with Republican challengers including Vice President JD Vance. Since the June ruling, Republican committees have blown past the former limits ahead of the midterms. The two Republican committees have [USN:L1N44I0OO TEXT:"exceeded"] the former national caps by more than $48 million, according to Federal Election Commission spending disclosures for July and August. Their Democratic counterparts also eclipsed the former limits, but by much less — just under $4 million. The three main national Republican committees ended August with about $233 million in cash. Their Democratic counterparts held roughly $130 million but also carried nearly $18 million in debt, according to Federal Election Commission filings.

item.title: Judge paves way for Michigan to add 2 midseason transfers
item.description: The procession of members of the high school class of 2022 to be able to compete in a fifth year of eligibility rolls on.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The procession of members of the high school class of 2022 to be able to compete in a fifth year of eligibility rolls on. Both former Miami (Fla.) tight end Alex Bauman and ex-Boise State defensive back Jeremiah Earby received a temporary restraining order and given a path to compete for the University of Michigan football team. Judge Julia B. Owdziej, ruling for the 22nd Washtenaw County Circuit Court in Ann Arbor, Mich., granted each a temporary restraining order on Tuesday for both players who were in the transfer portal. Bauman and Earby are currently enrolled at Michigan but have not officially signed, according to reports, while CBS Sports was the first to report that Wolverines are adding the pair through the transfer portal. A Michigan spokesperson declined comment. According to court records, both players filed for the temporary restraining order on Sept. 25 and a preliminary injunction hearing has been scheduled for Nov. 4. Owdziej ruled that both players are eligible to play this season. She wrote that denying them eligibility would be "irreparable and severe," and the harm to the NCAA would be "negligible." The NCAA has not commented, although NCAA president Charlie Baker did respond to Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine's signing an executive order earlier this week, giving the state's colleges and universities the option to permit athletes who graduated from high school in 2022 to compete in the 2026-27 college academic year. "One elected official seeking to make their own rules for their own schools' advantage is a terrible way to run athletic competitions," Baker said, while also pushing Congress to pass the Protect College Sports Act, proposed federal legislation aimed at reforming college athletics. Bauman, a 6-foot-5, 250-pound tight end, amassed 18 receptions for 166 yards and a touchdown last season for the Miami. Prior to his time in Coral Gables, he played for three seasons at Tulane and had 63 career catches for 610 yards and 13 touchdowns. The 6-2, 186-pound Earby earned All-Mountain West second-team honors at Boise State last fall. He started for two seasons for the Broncos after playing for two years at California. Michigan is in unfamiliar territory in coach Kyle Whittingham's first season. They are 3-2 overall, but 0-2 in the Big Ten Conference after a 20-14 loss at Minnesota on Oct. 3. The Wolverines host Penn State on Saturday. Michigan has held roster spots open in the hopes that Bauman and Earby would be ruled eligible. --Field Level Media

item.title: Chiefs LT Josh Simmons returns to practice for first time since camp
item.description: Kansas City Chiefs left tackle Josh Simmons returned to practice on Wednesday for the first time since sustaining a back injury at training camp.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Kansas City Chiefs left tackle Josh Simmons returned to practice on Wednesday for the first time since sustaining a back injury at training camp. Coach Andy Reid said on Sept. 30 that Simmons has been sidelined by a bulging disc in his lower back. The 2025 first-round draft pick will be a limited participant, Reid said ahead of Wednesday's practice. "I'm just going to ease him back in," Reid said. "He's going to practice, but we'll be on a limited basis there." Simmons, 23, has missed all four games this season after playing in only eight (all starts) in 2025. He missed four games due to a personal matter and later went on injured reserve after having surgery on his wrist for a fracture and a dislocation, Reid said last December. Undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson has started in place of Simmons at left tackle. The Chiefs (4-0), coming off a bye week, host the Los Angeles Chargers (0-5) on Sunday. Reid said on Wednesday that wide receiver Rashee Rice would not participate in practice because of the hamstring injury sustained in Week 4 against the Las Vegas Raiders. "We'll see how it goes," Reid said of Rice's prospects for practicing later this week. "He's actually feeling pretty good as he goes here, so we'll see. Those things, you start dealing with hamstrings, and it could be a week, could be two weeks, you don't know, but I know he's eager to get back in." Rice, 26, has 13 receptions on 17 targets for 190 yards and one touchdown in four games (three starts) this season. For his career, Rice has 169 catches for 1,987 yards and 15 TDs in 32 regular-season games (23 starts). He had 26 receptions for 262 yards and one TD in four playoff games at the Chiefs won the Super Bowl in the 2023 season. Kansas City picked Rice in the second round in the 2023 NFL Draft out of SMU. --Field Level Media

item.title: Undercover documentary shows Reform UK candidates making racist, sexual and violent remarks
item.description: Several members of Nigel Farage's Reform UK Party, including elected local-level politicians, have been filmed making racist, sexual and violent remarks by undercover reporters for an upcoming TV documentary.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Several members of Nigel Farage's Reform UK Party, including elected local-level politicians, have been filmed making racist, sexual and violent remarks by undercover reporters for an upcoming TV documentary. Farage's party has in recent months slipped from first place in opinion polls after allegations about its finances, and as the governing Labour Party's popularity has rebounded under new their new leader, Prime Minister Andy Burnham. The footage from the ITV documentary "Undercover: A Year In Reform" showed one man calling Asian homeowners "parasites" and expressing anti-Muslim views while campaigning for Reform in local elections earlier this year. He was subsequently elected. ITV released extracts of its findings before the full documentary airs on October 18. Other covertly filmed footage included one candidate in those elections discussing burying pork chops in the ground as a possible way to stop a new mosque being built. Another candidate repeatedly used a derogatory term for people from Pakistan and made explicit sexual comments about a fellow Reform member. Both were later elected. A fourth person, also a Reform councillor, was shown saying he wanted to "take out" illegal migrants entering Britain. Another councillor told an undercover reporter he was "so, so far-right, it's unbelievable" and wanted to train young men in military tactics to round up immigrants. Reform said in response to the footage: "Where members, activists and councillors have clearly behaved inappropriately, investigations have commenced. In some cases, there have been suspensions and due process must be followed. "Reform UK has improved and prioritised its vetting procedures, but from time to time, a handful of individuals who do not share our values will initially make it through vetting." Polls show Reform, an anti-immigrant party which was set up by Farage and was formerly known as the Brexit Party, has slipped back into second place behind Labour ahead of an election due in 2029. Police are investigating Reform for several potential offences under laws governing donations to political parties, and said in September they would also [USN:L8N4511I5 TEXT:"look into allegations"] that officials planned to break electoral law on foreign funding. The party denies any wrongdoing over its finances.

item.title: Não há evidências de que foto de ato pró-Lula na avenida Paulista seja IA
item.description: Não há evidências de que uma foto aérea do ato em apoio ao presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), candidato à reeleição, realizado no último domingo na avenida Paulista, em São Paulo, tenha sido alterada ou gerada por IA.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Não há evidências de que uma foto aérea do ato em apoio ao presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), candidato à reeleição, realizado no último domingo na avenida Paulista, em São Paulo, tenha sido alterada ou gerada por IA. No Facebook , posts exibem a foto do evento pró-Lula com a etiqueta “imagem alterada com IA” ao lado de uma imagem de uma multidão de amarelo, tratada nas publicações como “imagem original”. Ferramentas de detecção do Google e da OpenAI não encontraram marcas d’agua de uso de modelos de IA dessas empresas na imagem da manifestação de Lula. Já os detalhes da suposta “imagem original” são inconsistentes com registros de manifestações bolsonaristas realizadas na avenida Paulista nos últimos anos. A Reuters não encontrou a imagem na imprensa ou em perfis bolsonaristas. Na alegada foto do ato bolsonarista, há um trio elétrico preto, que tem uma cobertura amarela e o número 22 na lateral, estacionado em frente ao Museu de Arte de São Paulo Assis Chateaubriand (Masp). O candidato a presidente Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) participou de um evento de campanha na Paulista em 7 de setembro. Fotos da Reuters e uma transmissão ao vivo do site Poder360 indicam que não havia um carro de som semelhante ao da foto naquela manifestação. Também não há registros desse trio elétrico em imagens de atos bolsonaristas divulgadas pela imprensa em março de 2026; agosto e setembro de 2025; fevereiro e setembro de 2024; e setembro de 2022 . LULA As características da foto do ato de Lula, que foi divulgada pela sua campanha , coincidem com imagens e vídeos da manifestação deste final de semana. O trio elétrico vermelho, com o slogan de campanha do petista e a cobertura amarela, além de outros detalhes , aparece em fotos registradas pela Reuters no último domingo. O veículo também está visível na transmissão ao vivo feita pelo PT no YouTube e em uma gravação da Guarda Civil Metropolitana de São Paulo divulgada pelo Poder360 , assim como em imagens reproduzidas pela CNN Brasil e pela GloboNews . VEREDICTO Sem evidências. Não há indícios de que uma foto do ato pró-Lula tenha sido gerada por IA. Detalhes coincidem com imagens feitas pela imprensa e não existem registros anteriores da alegada "foto original". Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. item.title: Vídeo mostra trecho final da avenida Paulista para afirmar que ato pró-Lula estava vazio
item.description: Posts nas redes sociais usam imagens aéreas do trecho final da avenida Paulista, em São Paulo, entre as ruas Augusta e Bela Cintra, para afirmar que o ato em apoio ao presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) realizado no último domingo estava vazio.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Posts nas redes sociais usam imagens aéreas do trecho final da avenida Paulista, em São Paulo, entre as ruas Augusta e Bela Cintra, para afirmar que o ato em apoio ao presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) realizado no último domingo estava vazio. No entanto, a manifestação se concentrou em outro trecho da avenida, e registros feitos pela imprensa, pela prefeitura de São Paulo e por militantes mostram vários quarteirões da avenida lotados durante a marcha. "Desmascarando a esquerda. Lula proíbe contagem da USP e impede estimativa de público em ato na Paulista, mas drone registra vídeo da avenida", diz a legenda de uma postagem com as imagens no Instagram . O vídeo gravado de cima mostra uma reunião de pessoas usando vermelho, mas com partes da avenida vazias, um pouco antes da rua Augusta até a Bela Cintra , como confirmam imagens do Google Street View . A Reuters não conseguiu localizar a origem do vídeo checado, mas identificou nas imagens a mesma faixa com a frase "O Brasil se une por Lula" que foi estendida na Paulista na manifestação de domingo. Trata-se de uma faixa feita pela União Nacional dos Estudantes (UNE), pela União Brasileira dos Estudantes Secundaristas (Ubes) e pela Associação Nacional de Pós-Graduandos (ANPG), como mostra um registro mais próximo capturado pela Folha de S.Paulo . A UNE disse à Reuters que usou a faixa pela primeira vez na manifestação do domingo passado. Também afirmou que, no vídeo verificado, militantes estão retirando-a da avenida. A imprensa noticiou que os apoiadores de Lula se reuniram principalmente em sete quarteirões da avenida , à esquerda e à direita do Museu de Arte de São Paulo Assis Chateaubriand (Masp), da rua Haddock Lobo até a alameda Joaquim Eugênio de Lima -- portanto, no sentido oposto da Paulista ao mostrado no vídeo checado. Além disso, apoiadores e a campanha de Lula , além da imprensa (como a Reuters e o g1 ) e da Guarda Civil Metropolitana (GCM), da prefeitura de São Paulo, registraram a manifestação, demonstrando que havia uma concentração de pessoas bastante superior à que aparece nas imagens checadas. O Monitor do Debate Político da Universidade de São Paulo (USP) e o site Poder360 , que costumam estimar o público em manifestações políticas, afirmaram que a campanha de Lula não autorizou o sobrevoo de drones para a contagem. VEREDICTO Enganoso. O conteúdo mostra o trecho final da avenida Paulista, onde não havia grande concentração de pessoas, e não exibe os pontos da via onde havia mais participantes do ato pró-Lula no último domingo. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. Envie sugestões de checagem via WhatsApp pelo número (11) 91599-9278 . item.title: CoreWeave CEO notes strong backlog in memo to reassure staff over market scrutiny
item.description: CoreWeave CEO Mike Intrator said on Wednesday market can sometimes "misunderstand and act irrationally", with shares of the AI cloud-computing provider closing down around 15%.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: CoreWeave (CRWV.O) CEO Mike Intrator said on Wednesday market can sometimes "misunderstand and act irrationally", with shares of the AI cloud-computing provider closing down around 15%. Here are some details: The company's deal backlog is large enough to more than support its debt obligations, Intrator told employees in a memo that was seen by Reuters Issues such as the difficulties and delays observed in the attempted IPOs and debt financings of some of CoreWeave's rivals "are bleeding into the narrative around CoreWeave", Intrator said in the memo According to Bloomberg News, which first reported on the remarks earlier in the day, CoreWeave's bonds have plunged to levels that typically indicate distress CoreWeave's unsecured debt due in 2032 traded below 80 cents on the dollar on Wednesday, Bloomberg News said in a separate report citing Trace pricing data CoreWeave has reported revenue [USN:L4N4481ER TEXT:"backlog of $104.2 billion"] in the second quarter, up from $99.4 billion in the first quarter On top of the backlog, the company said it had secured more than $25 billion of net new customer commitments in the third quarter

item.title: Nasdaq fecha com forte queda, conforme dados sobre inflação alimentam temores de alta dos juros
item.description: Dados de inflação acima do esperado levaram o Nasdaq a um fechamento em forte queda nesta quarta-feira, com as preocupações sobre novos aumentos nas taxas de juros pelo Federal Reserve prejudicando as ações da Oracle, da CoreWeave e de outras empresas de IA sensíveis ao aumento dos custos de financiamento.
item.dc:creator: Noel Randewich
item.content:encoded: Dados de inflação acima do esperado levaram o Nasdaq a um fechamento em forte queda nesta quarta-feira, com as preocupações sobre novos aumentos nas taxas de juros pelo Federal Reserve prejudicando as ações da Oracle, da CoreWeave e de outras empresas de IA sensíveis ao aumento dos custos de financiamento. O aumento das apostas de que o Fed precisará de mais aumentos nas taxas para conter a inflação representou um duro golpe para algumas das empresas que mais valorizaram no mercado em 2026. A Oracle (ORCL.N) tombou 8,8%, enquanto as empresas de infraestrutura de IA CoreWeave (CRWV.O) e Nebius (NBIS.O) despencaram 15% e 10%, respectivamente. A Dell (DELL.N) e a Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE.N) caíram 11,4% e 8,2%, respectivamente, depois que o Barclays rebaixou a recomendação das fabricantes de servidores de IA de acima da média do mercado para neutro. O Índice de chips da Philadelphia SE (.SOX) caiu 4,3%, registrando queda pela sexta sessão consecutiva — sua maior sequência de perdas desde maio de 2025. Os preços ao consumidor nos EUA aceleraram em setembro, à medida que o custo da gasolina disparou e as pressões sobre os preços se estenderam para além do setor de energia, segundo dados do Bureau de Estatísticas do Trabalho do Departamento do Trabalho. Os operadores de taxas de juros estão precificando uma probabilidade de 37% de que os formuladores de política monetária do Fed aumentem as taxas neste mês, ante 22% na terça-feira, de acordo com a ferramenta FedWatch da CME. “Os investidores não estão satisfeitos com o relatório porque isso pressiona o Fed a aumentar as taxas para combater a inflação”, disse Adam Sarhan, diretor executivo da 50 Park Investments, em Nova York. “A inflação continua sendo o inimigo público número um para o mercado e para o Fed.” O S&P 500 recuou 1,11%, encerrando o pregão em 7.718,94 pontos, sua maior queda em um único dia desde 29 de julho. O Nasdaq caiu 1,88%, para 26.692,87 pontos, sua maior queda diária desde 23 de julho. O Índice Dow Jones Industrial Average teve queda de 0,09%, para 51.621,48 pontos. Oito dos 11 índices setoriais do S&P 500 registraram queda, liderados pelo setor de tecnologia da informação (.SPLRCT) , com baixa de 2,6%, seguido por uma perda de 1,78% no setor de serviços de comunicação (.SPLRCL) . Depois de atingir uma alta recorde na semana passada, o S&P 500 continua com alta de quase 13% em 2026, com a maior parte desse ganho impulsionado por ações relacionadas à IA. A mediana das ações do S&P 500 subiu 4% em 2026, e mais de 200 dos componentes do índice estão em território negativo. O Bank of America (BAC.N) caiu 4,8%. O lucro do banco diminuiu no terceiro trimestre, pois ele reservou US$1,2 bilhão para cobrir multas regulatórias por falhas na detecção de possíveis casos de lavagem de dinheiro. O Morgan Stanley (MS.N) caiu quase 3%, apesar de um aumento no lucro trimestral. O índice S&P 500 Banks (.SPXBK) recuou 0,7%, atingindo seu menor fechamento desde junho. Antes da divulgação dos dados sobre a inflação, a vice-chair de Supervisão do Fed, Michelle Bowman, afirmou que o banco central tinha tempo para aguardar e observar como os mercados e a economia evoluiriam após o aumento da taxa de juros em setembro, antes de decidir sobre novas medidas. A Bending Spoons (BSP.O) disparou 41% depois que a Berkshire Hathaway (BRKa.N) investiu mais US$330 milhões na proprietária do Vimeo e da AOL — um grande endosso do investidor de grande visibilidade, cujos movimentos são acompanhados de perto pelos operadores de mercado.

item.title: 米国株式市場＝ナスダック大幅安、インフレ加速で利上げ懸念
item.description:
Noel Randewich
［１４日 ロイター］ - 米国株式市場はナスダック総合指数が大幅安で取引を終えた。この日...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米国株式市場＝ナスダック大幅安、インフレ加速で利上げ懸念 5:10 配信

2021年10月18日撮影。 REUTERS/Tom Bergin//File Photo

Noel Randewich

［１４日　ロイター］ - 米国株式市場はナスダック総合指数が大幅安で取引を終えた。この日発表された９月の消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）が予想を上回り、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）による追加利上げへの懸念が強まった。

借り入れコスト上昇の影響を受けやすいオラクル、コアウィーブ、ネビウスなど人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株が売り込まれた。オラクルは８．８％安、コアウィーブとネビウスはそれぞれ１５％、１０％下落した。

ＡＩサーバーメーカーのデル・テクノロジーズとヒューレット・パッカード・エンタープライズはそれぞれ１１．４％、８．２％下落。バークレイズが両社の投資判断を「オーバーウエート」から「イコールウエート」に引き下げた。

フィラデルフィア半導体指数は４．３％下落し、６営業日続落。連続下落期間は２０２５年５月以来の長さとなった。

一方、アップルは０．５％上昇し、終値ベースの時価総額が初めて５兆ドルを上回った。

米労働省が１４日発表した９月ＣＰＩは前月比０．６％、前年比では３．７％上昇し、前月の０．４％と３．４％上昇から加速した。ガソリン価格が急騰し、物価上昇圧力がエネルギー以外にも広がったことが背景。

ＣＭＥのフェドウオッチによると、金利先物市場が織り込む今月の利上げ確率は３７％と、１３日の２２％から上昇した。

５０パーク・インベストメンツのアダム・サーハン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は「今回の統計は、インフレ抑制に向け利上げするようＦＲＢに圧力をかけるため、投資家は歓迎していない」と指摘。「インフレは引き続き、市場とＦＲＢにとって最大の敵だ」と述べた。

Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種の下落率は７月２９日以来の大きさとなった。

ナスダック総合は７月２３日以来の大幅な下落率を記録した。ダウ工業株３０種は小幅に下落した。

Ｓ＆Ｐ５００の主要１１セクターのうち８セクターが下落。情報技術が２．６％安と下げを主導した。通信サービスも下げが目立った。

米取引所の合算出来高は１８０億株。直近２０営業日の平均は１７６億株。

Ｓ＆Ｐ５００は先週、最高値を付けており、年初来の上昇率はなお１３％近い。上昇の大部分はＡＩ関連株がけん引している。構成銘柄の年初来騰落率の中央値は４％上昇にとどまり、２００銘柄以上が値下がりしている。

金融大手バンク・オブ・アメリカ（ＢｏｆＡ）は４．８％下落した。マネーロンダリング（資金洗浄）の疑いがある取引を検知できなかったことに対する規制当局の制裁金に関連し、１２億ドルの費用を計上し、第３・四半期は減益となった。モルガン・スタンレーは四半期決算が増益だったにもかかわらず、３％近く下落した。

Ｓ＆Ｐ５００銀行株指数は０．７％下落し、終値で６月以来の安値を付けた。

イタリアの情報技術（ＩＴ）企業ベンディング・スプーンズは４１％急伸した。動画共有サービスのＶｉｍｅｏやインターネットサービスのＡＯＬを傘下に持つ同社に、バークシャー・ハサウェイが３億３０００万ドルを追加出資した。市場参加者が動向を注視する著名投資会社からの強い支持を示すものとなった。

Ｓ＆Ｐ５００では値下がり銘柄数が値上がり銘柄数を１．１対１の比率で上回った。

item.title: Anthropic to add US voting information to Claude before midterms
item.description: Anthropic said on Wednesday it would add official US voting information from nonprofit Democracy Works and election results to its Claude AI chatbot later this month, ahead of the November midterms.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Anthropic said on Wednesday it would add official US voting information from nonprofit Democracy Works and election results to its Claude AI chatbot later this month, ahead of the November midterms. The AI company said its goal was to position Claude as a useful tool for political conversations, while preventing election-related abuse. "Today, conversations that touch broadly on politics, public policy or social issues account for about 5.75% of all conversations in the United States on Claude.ai, our consumer app," the company said in a statement, citing analysis of 250,000 US conversations. The move comes as AI companies increasingly position chatbots as sources of news and information, potentially helping Anthropic draw more users during the election cycle. About 0.51% of Claude conversations are specifically about elections or voting, Anthropic said, adding that it expects political and election-related queries to rise as election day approaches. Later this month, US users seeking voting logistics will receive answers drawn directly from Democracy Works’ database of state and local election sources. Anthropic said requests for recommendations on how to vote were extremely rare, accounting for just 0.01% of U.S. conversations.

item.title: Perella Weinberg, Piper Sandler abandon merger talks, source says
item.description: Investment bank Piper Sandler and advisory firm Perella Weinberg Partners have abandoned talks for an all-stock merger as they could not agree on financial and personnel terms, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Abigail Summerville
item.content:encoded: Investment bank Piper Sandler (PIPR.N) and advisory firm Perella Weinberg Partners (PWP.O) have abandoned talks for an all-stock merger as they could not agree on financial and personnel terms, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters on Wednesday. Shares of Perella Weinberg closed 19.1% lower at $13, while those of Piper Sandler ended up 0.96% at $64.5. Perella Weinberg declined to comment, while Piper Sandler did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. The Financial Times first reported on Wednesday that the merger talks fell through. The Wall Street Journal had reported last month that Piper Sandler was in talks to buy Perella Weinberg, which had a market value of about $1.4 billion at the time. A $485-million merger between Minneapolis-based Piper Jaffray and New York-based Sandler O'Neill led to the formation of Piper Sandler Companies in January 2020, creating a major investment bank specializing in the middle market, with leading advisory practices in financial services, healthcare and energy. Meanwhile, Perella Weinberg was founded by veteran Wall Street bankers Joseph Perella, Peter Weinberg and Terry Meguid in 2006. The firm went public in 2021 through a merger with a blank-check company backed by banking entrepreneur Betsy Cohen, in a deal valued at about $975 million.

item.title: Fed's Goolsbee says September CPI data was discouraging - Yahoo Finance
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Austan Goolsbee said on Wednesday the latest consumer-level inflation data left him worried about the state of price pressures.
item.dc:creator: Michael Derby
item.content:encoded: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Austan Goolsbee said on Wednesday the latest consumer-level inflation data left him worried about the state of price pressures. The September [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"consumer price index"] data, which showed higher-than-expected price pressures, was “discouraging,” Goolsbee said in an interview with Yahoo Finance. When it comes to the price pressure data, “I'm concerned, related to not just the overall number, but if you break out the components, services inflation shows little sign of improvement,” the official said, while affirming the central bank will get inflation back to its 2% target. Goolsbee stopped short of saying how he thinks the central bank should respond with rate policy in the near term while saying in strong terms that the Fed can't allow high price pressures to persist. If inflation pressures remain elevated, "there's not ambiguity about what, how the central bank has to deal with that," he said. "You must prevent the buildup of overheating, because if you get overheating buildup on the demand side, that tends to be very persistent and hard to get rid of," Goolsbee said. The Fed raised its interest rate target by a quarter percentage point last month to between 3.75% and 4% and penciled in an additional increase by the end of the year, as it works to get inflation to its 2% target. Key Fed officials have [USN:S0N44V01O TEXT:"waved"] markets off expectations of a rate hike at the Federal Open Market Committee meeting set for the end of the month, though the release of the CPI data put new life into market expectations that the central bank may move again sooner rather than later. In the interview, Goolsbee explained that the inflation data showed that price pressures are high even in the areas outside those directly impacted by things like tariffs, which is in part why he found the latest report to be so vexing. "This month's reading is over 5% for services inflation and you can't really attribute services inflation to tariffs, to oil prices, or things like that," Goolsbee said. "On the ground here in the Midwest, everywhere we're going, we're hearing about costs and we're hearing about prices," Goolsbee said. "There's very little that we're hearing that sounds like downturn, risks of recession and things like that, so that makes you more nervous about demand side overheating than just straight supply shock." The Fed has failed to get inflation back to its 2% target for over five years, though officials say market and public expectations data shows continued confidence that price pressures will be brought under control.

item.title: What is Starshield, SpaceX's military version of Starlink?
item.description: Ukraine said on Wednesday that Elon Musk's SpaceX had restricted military-grade Starlink services, hampering Ukrainian drone strike missions and air defenses.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ukraine said on Wednesday that Elon Musk's [USN:L8N4600M6 TEXT:"SpaceX had restricted "military-grade" Starlink services"], hampering Ukrainian drone strike missions and air defenses. The complaint has drawn renewed attention to the distinction between Starlink, SpaceX's commercial satellite internet service, and Starshield, a military version developed for the Pentagon. While Musk has said the two systems are separate, in many cases they share the same underlying satellite technology. "Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government," Musk said on Wednesday in a post on X, adding that any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military or the president. "Starlink is a commercial service owned and controlled by SpaceX. Usage of Starlink is limited to civilian or defensive activities and cannot be used for offensive military action, as doing so would be inappropriate for a commercial company." WHAT IS STARLINK? Starlink, the main profit engine of SpaceX (SPCX.O) , is a satellite internet network of more than 11,000 satellites that beam broadband service directly to user terminals about the size of a folded newspaper. Its roughly 13 million subscribers range from households and hikers to shipping companies and major airlines. Since launching its first Starlink satellites in 2019 aboard reusable SpaceX rockets, the company has built a vast low-Earth-orbit constellation that blankets much of the planet, delivering faster connections than traditional communications satellites, which typically operate much farther from Earth and in far smaller numbers. Starlink gave Ukraine a critical communications advantage early in the war, reshaping how militaries operate on the battlefield. But Musk has restricted Starlink for certain military uses while highlighting Starshield, a more secure network developed for government and military missions. WHAT IS STARSHIELD? Starshield is a SpaceX business unit that develops military and intelligence satellite systems for the Pentagon. While its missions are separate from Starlink's commercial broadband service, the distinction is not always clear-cut: Starshield's secure communications services use enhanced encryption and dedicated terminals, but rely on the vast Starlink constellation as their backbone. Starshield leverages the technology, engineering and operational experiences of Starlink, according to SpaceX. In addition to secure communications, the company says the militarized version can also provide users with Earth observation and the ability to integrate sensors or other payloads. The Pentagon, Starshield's largest customer, has spent billions of dollars on both Starlink and Starshield services. It has also bought dedicated Starshield satellites, including communications spacecraft for missile-warning missions and a spy constellation for the National Reconnaissance Office, Reuters reported in 2024. Questions over the relationship between Starlink and Starshield have persisted since [USN:L1N31S38K TEXT:"Russia threatened Western satellites supporting Ukraine in 2022"]. SpaceX unveiled Starshield later that year, but the secrecy surrounding national security space programs has left the precise boundaries between the two systems opaque. Those distinctions became a point of contention earlier this year when the [USN:L6N41W1B2 TEXT:"Pentagon clashed with SpaceX over higher prices for satellite services"] used by military drones during the Iran conflict, Reuters reported. SpaceX argued that some customers paying roughly $5,000 per terminal for Starlink should instead have been using a Starshield service costing about $25,000 per terminal. [USN:L6N4290XG TEXT:"Britain has also adopted Starshield"]. Under that arrangement, the service uses the same satellite constellation, ground stations and terrestrial infrastructure as Starlink, but operates through dedicated terminals and separate network gateways, Britain’s defence ministry has told Reuters. Other US partners are evaluating the system as well. New Zealand is doing a trial of Starshield to assess its usefulness for military operations, the New Zealand Defence Force previously told Reuters.

WASHINGTON, Oct 14 : Ukraine said on Wednesday that Elon Musk's SpaceX had restricted "military-grade" Starlink services, hampering Ukrainian drone strike missions and air defenses. The complaint has drawn renewed attention to the distinction between Starlink, SpaceX's commercial satellite internet service, and Starshield, a military version developed for the Pentagon. While Musk has said the two systems are separate, in many cases they share the same underlying satellite technology. "Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government," Musk said on Wednesday in a post on X, adding that any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military or the president. "Starlink is a commercial service owned and controlled by SpaceX. Usage of Starlink is limited to civilian or defensive activities and cannot be used for offensive military action, as doing so would be inappropriate for a commercial company." WHAT IS STARLINK?

Starlink, the main profit engine of SpaceX, is a satellite internet network of more than 11,000 satellites that beam broadband service directly to user terminals about the size of a folded newspaper. Its roughly 13 million subscribers range from households and hikers to shipping companies and major airlines. Since launching its first Starlink satellites in 2019 aboard reusable SpaceX rockets, the company has built a vast low-Earth-orbit constellation that blankets much of the planet, delivering faster connections than traditional communications satellites, which typically operate much farther from Earth and in far smaller numbers. Starlink gave Ukraine a critical communications advantage early in the war, reshaping how militaries operate on the battlefield. But Musk has restricted Starlink for certain military uses while highlighting Starshield, a more secure network developed for government and military missions. WHAT IS STARSHIELD?  Starshield is a SpaceX business unit that develops military and intelligence satellite systems for the Pentagon.  While its missions are separate from Starlink's commercial broadband service, the distinction is not always clear-cut: Starshield's secure communications services use enhanced encryption and dedicated terminals, but rely on the vast Starlink constellation as their backbone. Starshield leverages the technology, engineering and operational experiences of Starlink, according to SpaceX. In addition to secure communications, the company says the militarized version can also provide users with Earth observation and the ability to integrate sensors or other payloads. The Pentagon, Starshield's largest customer, has spent billions of dollars on both Starlink and Starshield services. It has also bought dedicated Starshield satellites, including communications spacecraft for missile-warning missions and a spy constellation for the National Reconnaissance Office, Reuters reported in 2024. Questions over the relationship between Starlink and Starshield have persisted since Russia threatened Western satellites supporting Ukraine in 2022. SpaceX unveiled Starshield later that year, but the secrecy surrounding national security space programs has left the precise boundaries between the two systems opaque. Those distinctions became a point of contention earlier this year when the Pentagon clashed with SpaceX over higher prices for satellite services used by military drones during the Iran conflict, Reuters reported. SpaceX argued that some customers paying roughly $5,000 per terminal for Starlink should instead have been using a Starshield service costing about $25,000 per terminal. Britain has also adopted Starshield. Under that arrangement, the service uses the same satellite constellation, ground stations and terrestrial infrastructure as Starlink, but operates through dedicated terminals and separate network gateways, Britain’s defence ministry has told Reuters. Other US partners are evaluating the system as well. item.title: Former portfolio manager sues Fidelity after leaving for Michael Dell's family office
item.description: A former semiconductor fund manager at Fidelity Investment Management has sued its parent company FMR, claiming it refused to pay him a "multimillion-dollar" compensation package after he joined DFO Management, the family office of billionaire Dell Technologies founder Michael Dell.
item.dc:creator: Suzanne McGee
item.content:encoded: A former semiconductor fund manager at Fidelity Investment Management has sued its parent company FMR, claiming it refused to pay him a "multimillion-dollar" compensation package after he joined DFO Management, the family office of billionaire Dell Technologies (DELL.N) founder Michael Dell. The suit, filed by Adam Benjamin in the Suffolk Division of the Superior Court of Massachusetts, alleges that after Fidelity executives failed to persuade him to stay at the firm, the company "turned on a dime" and terminated him on July 10 of this year. Fidelity then imposed a non-compete clause, causing him to forfeit a compensation package totaling in the millions of dollars. "Rather than protecting any legitimate business interests, the provisions are being broadly misused by Fidelity as a retention tool or improper barrier/deterrent to" Benjamin's ability to pursue other professional opportunities, the lawsuit alleges. Fidelity declined to comment on the lawsuit, which was filed on Friday. Neither Benjamin nor his lawyers could be reached for comment. Non-compete agreements are common in the asset management industry. Benjamin managed the $48 billion Fidelity Select Semiconductors Portfolio, which is up 58% so far this year, compared to 13.3% for the S&P 500 (.SPX) index. Its average annual return of 37.4% over the last five years puts it in the top percentile of all comparable funds rated by Morningstar, which awarded the fund five stars and a gold medalist rating, its top score. Benjamin began working at DFO on October 1, the lawsuit said. He alleged that Fidelity's withholding of compensation rests on the false claim that he was joining a competitor. He said he has never worked for Fidelity's own family office business.

item.title: Bond trading weakens for US banks as interest rate volatility affects investors
item.description: A steep selloff in the bond market showed up in Wall Street bank earnings during the last quarter, with some banks showing weaker fixed income trading as high interest rate volatility during the quarter curbed demand for transactions.
item.dc:creator: Tatiana Bautzer
item.content:encoded: A steep [USN:L8N45N0KW TEXT:"selloff in the bond market"] showed up in Wall Street bank earnings during the last quarter, with some banks showing weaker fixed income trading as high interest rate volatility during the quarter curbed demand for transactions. During the quarter, Treasury yields reached [USN:L6N45S11R TEXT:"multi-decade highs"] with some days showing abrupt moves in the market as investors repriced their expectations for where interest rates will go. At Morgan Stanley, revenues from fixed income, currencies and commodities trading (FICC) fell 7% in the quarter from a year earlier. [USN:L4N45Z0V1 TEXT:"At JPMorgan"], the drop was 4% and at [USN:L4N4600WF TEXT:"Bank of America"], 17%. [USN:L4N45Z0U6 TEXT:"Goldman Sachs"] had flat revenues with FICC trading. Citi was the odd one out, increasing its revenue 4% from a year earlier. "Interest rates rose pretty furiously throughout the third quarter, and it was unexpected versus where the market was in the second quarter", said Morgan Stanley Chief Financial Officer Sharon Yeshaya. There was less demand for structured transactions and the widening of credit spreads was a challenge to investors that have bond portfolios. Benchmark 10-year yields showed their [USN:L6N45M19U TEXT:"biggest quarterly rise since 2009"] at the end of September. "Reduced client activity and changing market conditions, including a major shift in interest rates, significantly affected our leading FICC businesses, including credit, mortgages and municipals," according to Bank of America Chief Financial Officer Alastair Borthwick. At Citigroup, most of the 4% growth in FICC trading revenue came from foreign exchange business and spread products. Citi CEO Jane Fraser told analysts rates revenue "was pressured by the trading environment, but we saw good growth in forex and spread products, both stable revenue streams." Another effect of [USN:L1N45U12M TEXT:"rising long-term yields"] on the banks' balance sheets was the higher volume of unrealized losses in securities portfolios. [USN:L4N4600XY TEXT:"Bank of America, for example"], showed unrealized losses on its bond portfolio - mortgage-backed securities and US Treasury, government-agency bonds - at $109 billion in the quarter ended September, up from $85 billion at the end of June, as bond yields rose in the last quarter. The bulk of these securities were in held-to-maturity segment, which the bank does not intend to sell. EQUITIES SHINE The results contrasted with that from equities trading desks, which brought eye-popping revenue growth in the quarter. At Goldman Sachs, equity trading revenue rose 72%, with higher revenues in derivatives and financing. Morgan Stanley equity revenues grew 41% and JPMorgan's, 49%. Bank of America and Citi had the lowest equity trading revenues growth, 11% and 14%, respectively. Oppenheimer analyst Chris Kotowski sees increased risk in the reliance on equity revenues, that may be volatile. "We do fear that there is an 'easy come, easy go' risk with these revenues," he wrote in a note to clients.

item.title: 欧州市場サマリー（14日）
item.description:
＜ロンドン株式市場＞
上昇して取引を終えた。ＦＴＳＥ１００種は反発。米インフレ指標を受けてポンドが対ドルで下落したこ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
欧州市場サマリー（14日） 3:54 配信

＜ロンドン株式市場＞

上昇して取引を終えた。ＦＴＳＥ１００種は反発。米インフレ指標を受けてポンドが対ドルで下落したことが好感され、輸出関連株が買われた。中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数も０．０９％高と続伸した。

製薬大手アストラゼネカは３．４％、ＧＳＫは３．６％、それぞれ上昇した。

英日用品のユニリーバは２．５％、高級ブランド会社バーバリーは３．５％いずれも値上がりした。

ヒーリー英財務相は、予算案に盛り込む新施策に関し、国債発行には依存せず、増税もしくは歳出削減によって財源を確保する見通しだと報じられた。

イングランド銀行（英中央銀行）チーフエコノミストのピル氏は、市場で今後１年間に４回の利上げが見込まれていることに懐疑的な見方を示した。これを受けて、ＦＴＳＥ３５０種住宅建設株指数は３．２３％上昇。

一方、金などの値下がりで貴金属株指数 は３．５３％安。銀行株指数 は０．５８％下落した。

９月の米消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）は前年同月からの伸び率が加速し、市場予想を上回った。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞

小幅に反発して取引を終えた。半導体関連企業による強気な需要見通しを受け、人工知能（ＡＩ）を巡る懸念が和らいだ。

２０２６年７─９月期決算を発表したオランダの半導体製造装置メーカーＡＳＭＬホールディングは１．２％高。２９、３０年の発注に向けて顧客から関心が寄せられていると明らかにし、需要が堅調に推移する見通しが示された。

ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種ヘルスケア株指数は２．３１％高。ベルギーでの人員削減を発表した製薬大手ＧＳＫは３．６％上昇した。

一方、資源株指数は１．１８％安。ＪＰモルガンが目標株価を引き下げた貴金属採掘フレスニヨは４．６％下落した。

デンマークの風力発電大手オーステッドは３．９％安。米国の洋上風力発電所事業への懸念から、売られた。スウェーデンの銀行ＳＥＢは４．６％安。

ブレント原油先物価格は高値圏で推移。インフレへの懸念から、市場は欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）が１２月会合で追加利上げに踏み切るとの観測を強めている。

また、９月の米消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）は前年同月からの伸び率が加速し、市場予想を上回った。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞

域内国債利回りが上昇した。米国のインフレ加速で連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）の追加利上げ観測が強まり、米債利回りが上昇した動きに追随した。

米労働省労働統計局が発表した９月の米消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）は前月比０．６％、前年比では３．７％上昇し、前月の０．４％と３．４％上昇から加速した。ガソリン価格の急騰を背景に伸びが加速し、１０月中の米利上げの可能性が再び意識される状況となった。

クインテット・プライベート・バンクのチーフストラテジスト、ダニエレ・アントヌッチ氏は「総合とコアの双方でインフレが加速したことは、物価上昇圧力の持続性が強まっていることを示唆する」と指摘。「堅調な成長と相まって、これはわれわれがＦＲＢが年内の追加利上げに踏み切ると予想する理由の一つだ」と述べた。

米国経済の規模と重要性、ＦＲＢが他の中央銀行に及ぼす影響力を踏まえると、米金融政策を巡る見通しは他の世界の債券市場にも影響を与える傾向がある。

米ＣＰＩを受けて米債券利回りが上昇する中、ドイツ１０年債利回りもこれに追随し、２ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）上昇の３．４８１％となった。

独仏１０年債利回り格差は約１４０ｂｐ。１０月序盤には一時１５８ｂｐ超まで拡大していた。欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）のラガルド総裁は１４日、フランスは財政健全化を通じて自国の債務問題を解決すべきだと述べ、ＥＣＢによる債券市場への介入観測を事実上けん制した。

ＥＣＢは今年、２５ｂｐの利上げを２回実施している。短期金融市場は１２月の理事会までに追加利上げが実施されるとの見方を完全に織り込んでいる。

item.title: PSG down Man City 4-2 in pulsating Champions League clash
item.description: Twice-defending champions Paris St Germain beat Manchester City 4-2 in a pulsating Champions League encounter on Wednesday, their devastating first-half display proving decisive against a City side playing under a cloud of scrutiny.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing
item.content:encoded: Twice-defending champions Paris St Germain beat Manchester City 4-2 in a pulsating Champions League encounter on Wednesday, their devastating first-half display proving decisive against a City side playing under a cloud of scrutiny. On a breathless night featuring 46 goals, Bradley Barcola scored a hat-trick in Liverpool's 6-3 thrashing of LASK, Aston Villa recorded the biggest European victory in their history with a 6-0 thrashing of Fenerbahce and Real Madrid staged a stunning late comeback to beat AS Roma 4-3. But no fixture carried more intrigue than the Etihad clash, where City played their first home game since being found guilty of 114 breaches of financial rules. City, who have denied all wrongdoing and appealed the verdict, were carved open by PSG in the first half. PSG'S FIRST-HALF BLITZ Desire Doue and Ousmane Dembele scored less than two minutes apart before Warren Zaire-Emery's clever touch released Vitinha to drive the third beyond Gianluigi Donnarumma in the 32nd minute. City emerged transformed after the break and Erling Haaland headed in Iliman Ndiaye's cross in the 53rd minute to become the fastest player to reach 60 Champions League goals, hitting the landmark in 60 games compared with Lionel Messi’s previous record of 80. City's joy was short-lived as Maghnes Akliouche's stunning long-range strike found the net despite Donnarumma getting a hand to it. Haaland had the City fans on their feet when he swept home Ayyoub Bouaddi's pass in the 75th minute for his second, before Donnarumma made up for his blunder by saving a penalty from Ferran Torres. The match unfolded against an "us against the world" backdrop, with City fans in the South Stand holding up cards that read "CTID" (City Till I Die). Former City manager Pep Guardiola watched from the stands alongside chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak and senior executives Ferran Soriano and Hugo Viana. VILLA HIT FENERBAHCE FOR SIX At Villa Park, Nicolas Jackson and Ross Barkley both scored twice in a dominant display by the hosts. Johan Manzambi opened the scoring in the 12th minute before Jackson struck in the 31st and 39th minutes to give Villa a commanding halftime lead. Barkley added a fourth from the penalty spot in the 68th minute before grabbing his second four minutes later, while Tammy Abraham completed the rout with a stoppage-time strike. At the Stadio Olimpico, Real Madrid scored three times in the closing stages to overturn a two-goal deficit. Marten de Roon gave Roma the lead in the 20th minute before Kylian Mbappe equalised five minutes later, but Donyell Malen struck twice in the 51st and 57th minutes to put the hosts in control. However, the visitors mounted a remarkable comeback as Carlos Espi pulled a goal back in the 82nd minute before Endrick levelled three minutes later. Former Roma defender Antonio Ruediger then completed the turnaround in the 90th minute, holding off his marker to steer home Arda Guler's inswinging corner from close range and snatch victory for the Spanish side. Liverpool's Barcola, meanwhile, scored his first goals for the club with his hat-trick in their rout of Champions League newcomers LASK in Austria. Ronald Araujo, Jeremie Frimpong and Lewis Koumas also scored for Andoni Iraola's side, who bounced back from Sunday's 3-0 Premier League defeat by City. Florian Flecker struck twice for the hosts.

item.title: 燃料高で物価圧力強まる、雇用は横ばい傾向＝米地区連銀報告
item.description: [１４日 ロイター] - 米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が１４日発表した地区連銀経済報告（ベージュブック）で、米国の労働市場...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
燃料高で物価圧力強まる、雇用は横ばい傾向＝米地区連銀報告 3:46 配信

２０１９年３月撮影　REUTERS/Leah Millis

[１４日　ロイター] - 米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が１４日発表した地区連銀経済報告（ベージュブック）で、米国の労働市場は雇用も解雇も低水準にとどまる状態が続く一方、一部地域でインフレ圧力が強まっていることが示された。

地区連銀経済報告は「企業はディーゼル燃料（軽油）価格の高止まりを報告し、燃料サーチャージを通じてコスト上昇がサプライチェーン全体に転嫁されていると指摘した」と報告。物価動向について、１２地区連銀のうち３地区で全般的な価格上昇が「力強い」と報告され、８地区は「緩やか」と報告された。

雇用については、大半の地区で全体的な雇用水準にほとんど、もしくは全く変化がみられなかったと報告した。

全般的な経済活動は、２地区で「緩やかな」ペースで成長。３地区は「控えめ」なペース、４地区は「小幅な」成長を報告し、３地区では経済活動に大きな変化は見られなかった。国内の多くの地域で企業が景気見通しについて前向きな見方を維持していると報告されたが、「成長見通しは概して小幅なものにとどまり、製造業がけん引する一方で、根強い不確実性が重しとなっている」とした。

インフレが広範囲に波及するとの懸念が高まる中、軽油価格の高騰に関する言及は２１件だった。前回の報告の２件から大幅に増加した。ダラス地区連銀は「コスト上昇の要因として最も多く挙がったのが軽油で、貨物輸送や農業、航空運賃に影響し、多くの産業で利益率を圧迫している」と指摘した。複数の地区で「その他のコモディティー（商品）や関税、保険による価格圧力も続いている」との指摘もあった。

複数の地区連銀は大規模な解雇は見られないとしたが、５地区では退職者の補充見送りや採用手控えで人員を削減していると報告。いくつかの地区では、個人からの生活費上昇への対応や、福利厚生の拡充といった形でインフレが賃金上昇圧力となっていると報告された。

労働市場に対する人工知能（ＡＩ）の影響も示され、シカゴ地区連銀では、ＡＩ導入による生産性の向上に伴う雇用の削減が報告された。一方、ダラス地区連銀の人材派遣会社は、ＡＩ導入拡大を管理するために採用担当者を新規雇用したという。

住宅市場の低調も顕著になっており、フィラデルフィア地区連銀は「中古住宅販売は引き続き小幅に減少した」と報告。「９月の住宅ローン金利上昇により、住宅市場の活動はさらに鈍化した。借入コストの上昇で希望者が購入を手控える一方、売り出し物件の在庫は低水準にとどまっている」という。ニューヨーク地区連銀は、金利上昇が市場への住宅供給を抑制していると指摘。

ボストンやニューヨーク、ミネアポリス、サンフランシスコの各連銀では、悪化したカナダとの貿易関係も製造業や観光業の抑制要因として挙げられた。

今回の報告は１０月５日までに収集された情報に基づき、フィラデルフィア地区連銀が作成した。

ロイター 関連ニュース 〔アングル〕ＥＵの自動車現地調達ルール案、中国勢は先回りで足場固め コラム：「ウォール街」と実体経済の温度差、ＡＩブームで一層鮮明に アングル：金価格、米国債利回り上昇でも4000ドル台維持　中銀の準備資産分散が下支え アングル：ＡＩ関連の資金調達、低格付け領域にも拡大　投資家は警戒感強める コラム：ベセント氏の危うい賭け、ＡＩ主導の経済成長は「債務病」の特効薬ならず 最終更新: 10/15(木) 6:32 ロイター

item.title: Eight US states sue OpenAI, claiming ChatGPT harms young users
item.description: A bipartisan group of eight states said on Wednesday they had sued OpenAI in courts across the country over harms they say ChatGPT has caused to their residents, alleging the chatbot has coached its users — including teenagers — to harm themselves or others.
item.dc:creator: Diana Jones
item.content:encoded: A bipartisan group of eight states said on Wednesday they had sued OpenAI in courts across the country over harms they say ChatGPT has caused to their residents, alleging the chatbot has coached its users — including teenagers — to harm themselves or others. Attorneys general from the states, which include Iowa, Kansas and Arizona, filed the lawsuits independently in state courts, claiming ChatGPT is designed to be agreeable and engaging to earn the trust of users. But the chatbot reinforces delusions, encourages dangerous behavior and assists users in planning violence like mass shootings, the lawsuits claim. The lawsuits represent the most significant coordinated state action against an artificial intelligence company, adding to a wave of legal challenges OpenAI faces as it prepares for a public listing. Florida's attorney general filed the first such state [USN:L6N429106 TEXT:"suit"] in June. The lawsuits accuse the company of violating state consumer protection laws by misleading users about the safety of ChatGPT. The states also allege that the company created a public nuisance by endangering the health of their residents. The lawsuits seek orders forcing OpenAI to make changes to how ChatGPT works. Among other things, the states want the company barred from developing AI models that can improve themselves unless it can ensure those models are aligned with human values. The states, which also include Arkansas, Idaho, Montana, Nebraska and West Virginia, are also seeking civil monetary penalties for OpenAI's violations of state law as well as damages. A spokesperson for OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The company is also facing dozens of lawsuits by private plaintiffs, alleging ChatGPT helped users [USN:L6N45D0ZP TEXT:"plan mass shootings"] or other violence.

item.title: Pope Leo back on his feet after shock cancer diagnosis
item.description: Pope Leo's recovery from surgery is progressing as expected and he has begun walking in his hospital room, the Vatican said.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

Pope Leo back on his feet after shock cancer diagnosis

Pope Leo's recovery from surgery is progressing as expected and he has begun walking in his hospital room, the Vatican said.

Pope Leo arrives at Gemelli Hospital ahead of the pontiff's surgery to remove a lung nodule in Rome, Italy, on Oct 13, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Guglielmo Mangiapane)

FAST

VATICAN CITY: Pope Leo 's recovery from surgery is progressing as expected and he has begun walking in his hospital room and eating normally, the Vatican said on Wednesday (Oct 14), after doctors announced the 71-year-old pontiff was being treated for lung cancer . World leaders, Catholics across the globe and senior cardinals at the Vatican have offered prayers for Pope Leo after he had part of his right lung removed in an operation on Tuesday. Blood tests and a chest X-ray carried out on Wednesday showed normal post-operative results, the Vatican said, adding that the pontiff had undergone respiratory physiotherapy. The cancer diagnosis for a pope known to be relatively young and energetic and who was elected only in May 2025 caused shock and raised questions about the future shape of his papacy as he deals with the illness.

Pope Leo normally follows a very busy schedule. He is due to make a tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from Nov 6 to 17 and the Vatican press office said on Wednesday that "nothing has changed" regarding the planned trip. However, Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori said on Wednesday that the dates could change because of the amount of time his recovery would take. The pope is the ultimate earthly authority for the world 's 1.4 billion Catholics and does not have a deputy who steps in when he is sick. When a pope is incapacitated, the business of the Vatican's vast bureaucracy carries on as usual, holding off on any decisions that require papal approval.

PRAYERS FOR POPE LEO A prayer was recited for Pope Leo to have a good convalescence and complete healing during an open-air Mass in St Peter's Square on Wednesday following the surgery. The pope has been diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma, the most common form of lung cancer , and doctors removed the lower lobe of his right lung during Tuesday's operation in an effort to eliminate all cancer ous tissue. Human lung s have five lobes - three in the right lung and two in the left. The operation lasted about 90 minutes and was completed without complications, the pope 's lead surgeon, Professor Stefano Margaritora, and his personal physician, Dr Luigi Carbone, said late on Tuesday. The Vatican has not disclosed the size of the tumour or whether the disease had spread to nearby lymph nodes, key factors in determining prognosis. Dr Serena Ricciardi, a lung cancer specialist at Rome's San Camillo Forlanini Hospital, said that if the cancer had not spread to Pope Leo 's lymph nodes, the surgery may have been sufficient for treatment. "If there are no further issues or lymph node involvement, we could consider the surgery curative," she told Reuters. "The disease has been completely removed." Pope Leo is relatively young for a Church leader. He enjoys sports, including tennis, and is not known to be a smoker or to have had recent health issues.

Related:

What we know about Pope Leo's lung cancer diagnosis

Pope Leo recovering after lung cancer operation

ENGAGEMENTS CANCELLED UNTIL NEXT WEEK The Vatican said this week that the pope was expected to remain in hospital for about a week and that all his public engagements had been cancelled until Oct 20. The Mass on Wednesday was the closing act of an assembly of bishops called by Pope Leo to discuss the Church's family life teachings, the largest gathering of Church leaders so far during this papacy. Filipino Cardinal Luis Tagle led the service in place of Pope Leo . The pope last week approved Tagle as the dean of the Church's College of Cardinals, in the first selection of an Asian cleric to the elite role. Political leaders offered messages of support. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he and his wife Jeanette were praying for the pope , an American who was born in Chicago. "May the Lord give him strength and the Holy Spirit guide the medical professionals taking care of the Holy Father," he said on X. Rubio met Pope Leo at the Vatican in May. There was no immediate response on social media from US President Donald Trump, who has criticised the pope , or from Vice President JD Vance, who is a Catholic.

Source: Reuters/fs

item.title: Red hot CPI report fuels AI rout
item.description: NEW YORK, Oct 14 : Major AI stocks slumped on Wednesday following the latest hot US inflation report, highlighting investor concern about the risks posed by rising borrowing costs in this capital-intensive sector.Among the leading decliners were data center operator CoreWeave, which fell 16 per cent, AI infra

Red hot CPI report fuels AI rout

An AI (Artificial Intelligence) sign is seen at the World Artificial Intelligence Conference (WAIC) in Shanghai, China July 6, 2023. REUTERS/Aly Song/File Photo

FAST

NEW YORK, Oct 14 : Major AI stocks slumped on Wednesday following the latest hot US inflation report, highlighting investor concern about the risks posed by rising borrowing costs in this capital-intensive sector. Among the leading decliners were data center operator CoreWeave, which fell 16 per cent, AI infrastructure provider Nebius, off 11 per cent, cloud computing giant Oracle, down 9 per cent, and AI server seller Dell Technologies, down 11 per cent. Together the declines erased some $80 billion of market value.  The declines reflect the impact of tightening financial conditions, as well as the outsize gains scored by some of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom. Barclays on Wednesday downgraded Dell and two other enterprise hardware stocks, noting that Dell shares have quadrupled this year — part of an AI-fueled investor binge that has resulted in 16 stocks in the S&P 500 technology sector at least doubling this year, according to Reuters calculations. Concern over rising borrowing costs also weighed on Wednesday's other big decliners. Selling has been particularly intense in CoreWeave, which has issued $22 billion of bonds and $26 billion of loans, according to LSEG data. A CoreWeave bond that was issued in June yielding 9.625 per cent recently yielded 15 per cent.

"We're getting a whole lot of information suggesting that the largest AI companies may not be generating the earnings or revenue people anticipated, and I think that makes everyone nervous about companies like CoreWeave," said Kim Forrest, chief investment officer at Bokeh Capital Partners.  Coreweave Chief Executive Officer Mike Intrator said in an internal memo the market is acting “irrationally” and that he remains confident in the AI cloud company, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday. Wednesday's rout is the latest sign of a market struggling to come to grips with the implications of high inflation at a time when AI-fueled corporate borrowing has helped push up global interest rates. Investors generally remain sanguine on the sector in part because its largest players, from chip maker Nvidia to the so-called hyperscalers — primarily Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Amazon — are highly profitable and widely perceived as well managed, despite concerns about debt.  But higher rates will make borrowing and building costlier, a fact that is likely to hit unprofitable and less-profitable firms first. On Wednesday, US interest rates rose following the hot inflation report, pushing the 30-year yield as high as 5.63 per cent before rates pulled back sharply in the afternoon. "I do think long rates above 5 per cent and creeping towards 6 per cent is a problem for the marginal borrower, I'll call them," said Ross Mayfield, investment strategy analyst at Baird, in an interview with Reuters. "It gets a lot harder for the tiers below the kind of big four hyperscalers."  The Nasdaq was down 2 per cent on Wednesday afternoon, with Alphabet and the other major hyperscalers mostly down between around 2 per cent. SpaceX, another major AI player, was down 3 per cent. "I guess it's grown to a group of five now. SpaceX has kind of joined the party here to join in with like Meta and Microsoft and Google and Amazon," said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management. "Those five are spending like 75 per cent of the money that's being invested in data centers here in the country. And those five are obviously putting all their profits and then some into these data centers and the returns they're generating from those are really good." Despite the strong economics of these firms and their investments, Ellerbroek said it's not surprising that investors remain skeptical about the AI buildout, in part because of the busts that have preceded this one, particularly the dot-com meltdown that started in 2000. "This select group of companies is driving most of the growth in the economy and the stock market, and they're investing so, so aggressively and investors just aren't really willing to pay for it or fully buy in to the extent that we saw in the late 90s or whatever when investors kind of lost their minds," Ellerbroek said. "Investors have definitely not lost their minds. They're being very cautious and I think selective."

Source: Reuters

item.title: Racial employment gap widened among new US lawyers, study finds
item.description: Longstanding racial gaps in US entry-level lawyer employment increased for 2025 graduates, with white law graduates securing jobs at a higher rate than their Black, Hispanic and Asian classmates, new data show.
item.dc:creator: Karen Sloan
item.content:encoded: Longstanding racial gaps in US entry-level lawyer employment increased for 2025 graduates, with white law graduates securing jobs at a higher rate than their Black, Hispanic and Asian classmates, new data show. More than 94% of 2025’s white law graduates found jobs within 10 months, compared to less than 91% of law graduates of color, according to figures released Wednesday by the National Association for Law Placement. Black law graduates had the lowest employment rate at 87%, down from nearly 90% in 2024, the NALP data showed. The employment rate for 2025 Hispanic law graduates was slightly over 91%, down from more than 92% the previous year. The employment rate for Asian law graduates held steady at about 92%. The relatively small cohort of Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander law graduates posted the highest employment rate at more than 96%. “A law degree should open doors, but NALP's latest report shows that those doors are not equally open to everyone,” NALP Executive Director Nikia Gray said in a statement after releasing the data. The law graduates of 2025 hit the job market amid the Trump administration’s widespread campaign to eliminate diversity, equity and inclusion programs in higher education, government and the private sector. In March 2025, the US Equal Employment Opportunity Commission [USN:L1N3Q010H TEXT:"demanded detailed hiring data from 20 major firms"], including applicant names and whether race or gender influenced their employment decisions. The US Federal Trade Commission earlier this year [USN:FWN3YV125 TEXT:"warned"] 42 major law firms that their hiring practices may violate federal antitrust law. Diversity Lab, a group that promoted diversity goals at law firms, [USN:L6N42D0S9 TEXT:"shuttered"] in June after coming under FTC scrutiny. Many major law firms have publicly withdrawn or altered their public references to diversity, equity and inclusion since Trump returned to the White House, a Reuters special report found . Nearly 50 US law firms that previously provided NALP with demographic data about their lawyers [USN:L6N40C159 TEXT:"declined to do so"] this year, with NALP attributing the drop to Trump’s crackdown on law firm DEI efforts. Additionally, the US Department of Education is [USN:L6N44I0V8 TEXT:"poised to revoke"] the American Bar Association’s status as the federally recognized accreditor of US law schools, partly because it says the ABA took too long to eliminate DEI standards for schools. According to the new NALP data, white law graduates outpaced every racial group except for Middle Eastern or North African law graduates in securing jobs that require passing the bar — considered the gold standard for legal employment. First-generation college students had a lower employment rate than law graduates whose parents attended college or law school. AI-powered stock funds bet bots can pick stocks faster and better than humans

FAST

PROVIDENCE, Rhode Island, Oct 14 : A handful of fund managers are betting that exchange traded funds run by AI stock-picking models can crunch data quicker and make better investment decisions than humans, even as many people remain wary or even fearful of artificial intelligence. So far, fewer than half-a-dozen ETFs, collectively managing only about $30 million of the ETF industry's nearly $17 trillion in assets, rely solely on AI-powered bots to control everything from research to stock selection. While that represents a tiny fraction of the industry, AI is making its way slowly and steadily into the investment processes of most asset managers, to some extent, even if that may not yet be visible to investors themselves. Earlier this year, 91 per cent of asset managers surveyed by Mercer reported plans to increase their use of AI-based portfolio management tools this year and said they are trying to figure out what tasks can be safely handed off to AI.      The performance of the handful of funds that rely solely on AI to generate returns shows they are beating the market, even if their track records stretch back only a few months. Their managers argue these returns will attract more investments into the idea over time.

"Until now you've had two choices: be a passive investor and own an index, or be an active investor" with a human picking stocks, said Tal Schwartz, founder and CEO of Ai Funds. "I want to offer a third option: where it's AI that is doing it all for you."  In August, Schwartz launched the High Conviction US Equity AI-Managed ETF, built on a proprietary AI learning algorithm that analyzes decades of market data. So far, it has attracted less than $20 million in assets, according to data from ETF.com, but Schwartz said it is still early days. AI can crunch more data more rapidly than any human being, he said, and strips human emotions and cognitive biases out of the investment process.  "I know this is a long-term process, that people will only become convinced over time," he added. "I think that what will convince them is performance." Schwartz's fund is up 2.7 per cent since its August 21 launch, beating the 1.1 per cent gain for the S&P 500 index in the same time frame. Two funds launched by Israeli asset manager FinQ in February have handily beaten the 11.0 per cent gain by the S&P over that time frame. FinQ's dollar-neutral US Large-Cap AI-managed ETF has soared 25.35 per cent and the version of the ETF not offering a currency hedge is 23.98 per cent higher since inception. Two other funds, the Pacer S&P 500 3AI Top 100 ETF and the Pacer S&P World 3AI Top 100 ETF, are ahead 10.34 per cent and 10.33 per cent, respectively, since their launches in early May, compared to a gain of 5.8 per cent for the S&P 500. Nonetheless, advisers and analysts said the funds' short track records and above-average fees may limit investor interest.  "Advisers are comfortable with AI that informs a decision and uneasy with AI that makes it," said Jeff Judge, a financial adviser at Chesapeake Financial Planners in Forest Hill, Maryland, adding his clients are not clamoring for this. "Proof that this approach works will really come down to who can thoughtfully manage risk and ride out a down market," said Todd Sohn, ETF analyst at Strategas. AI-ENHANCED ETFS MORE COMMON Other firms have rolled out "AI-enhanced" ETFs, which use AI to undertake quantitative analysis, analyze stocks or monitor risk. This cautious approach is more common, insiders said. "We've been training models using AI for seven or eight years now, and using them to run live capital for about four years," said David Wright, head of quantitative investments at Pictet Asset Management in Geneva. His firm launched the Pictet AI Enhanced US Equity ETF in February. Since its debut, the fund has attracted $163 million in assets and posted gains of 14.8 per cent, compared to 11.4 per cent for the S&P 500. Wright compares using AI in the investment process to using a plane's autopilot functions. The autopilot may be able to take off, cruise and land with no humans involved, but, he added, "I wouldn't go on a plane that didn't have a pilot." Other asset managers are taking a similarly cautious approach to integrating AI.  "I'm not losing any sleep over robots ending the world," said Dan Taylor, deputy chief investment officer of systematic within Man Group, referring to recent headlines. "But I still do worry about AI's ability to deal with the most extreme, unlikely events, where all the action happens, both good and bad."

Source: Reuters

item.title: Patriots open window for A.J. Brown; Christian Gonzalez also limited in return
item.description: New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown was a limited participant on Wednesday as the team opened his 21-day practice window.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown was a limited participant on Wednesday as the team opened his 21-day practice window. Brown has been sidelined since sustaining a high-ankle sprain during the second half of the Patriots' 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks in the teams' season opener on Sept. 9. He went on injured reserve two days later and missed the team's last four games. Pro Bowl cornerback Christian Gonzalez also was limited after telling reporters before practice that he's ready to return to the field after missing two games due to a shoulder injury. "I'm good now, ready for Sunday," Gonzalez told reporters. The Patriots (3-2) host their AFC East rivals, the New York Jets (2-3), on Sunday. New England cornerbacks Carlton Davis III (neck) and Karon Prunty (hamstring) were the only players who did not practice, while quarterback Drake Maye (right shoulder) was a full participant. Brown and Gonzalez were among 13 players listed as limited, including running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) and offensive tackles Will Campbell (knee) and Morgan Moses (foot). Gonzalez, 24, signed a four-year, $135 million contract extension last month. He has started all 37 career games in which he has played -- including three this season -- since being selected by New England with the 17th overall pick of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Oregon. As for Brown, he sustained his injury after he was targeted by a third-down pass from Maye, but Seahawks nickel cornerback Nehemiah Pritchett deflected the pass to force a punt. Pritchett's knee landed on the outside of Brown's ankle, which twisted inward as he went to the ground. Acquired from the Philadelphia Eagles via trade in early June, Brown had three receptions for a team-high 26 yards in the first half. Brown, 29, was named second-team All-Pro with the Eagles in 2022, 2023 and 2024. He has 527 receptions for 8,055 yards and 56 touchdowns in 106 career games (98 starts) with the Tennessee Titans (2019-21), Eagles (2022-25) and Patriots. --Field Level Media

WASHINGTON, Oct 14 : A group of Democratic lawmakers on Wednesday urged the Federal Aviation Administration to conduct a new environmental review before allowing an Amazon Prime Air drone delivery hub to be located about 30 miles (48.28 km) west of Boston. Massachusetts Democratic US Senators Ed Markey and Elizabeth Warren and Representatives Jim McGovern and Lori Trahan wrote to FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford seeking a new review after communities raised concerns about the planned Westborough hub and its impact on the environment and residents’ quality of life, including noise pollution, health and safety, and privacy. The FAA said it would respond directly to the lawmakers. Amazon did not immediately comment. Here are more details:

• On September 28, a group of 15 states and a Texas county on Monday sued the FAA over the agency's environmental review of planned commercial drone package delivery rules. • The agency in July issued a broad environmental review that allows qualifying drone operators to launch fleets without a site-specific environmental analysis. • The states — including New York, California, Massachusetts, Wisconsin and Michigan — and Harris County, Texas, said the FAA violated the law by failing to adequately analyze the potential environmental impacts of expanded drone package delivery operations. • Drone delivery operations are already happening in states including California, Texas, Arkansas, Florida and Utah under the waiver process. • The FAA said last year that eliminating the need for waivers "will significantly expand the use-case for drone technologies in areas like: manufacturing, farming, energy production, filmmaking, and the movement of products including lifesaving medications." • The FAA environmental review included reviewing the noise impacts of 1,150 average drone deliveries from a single hub. Drones would depart a hub and travel en route at an altitude of less than 400 feet (121 meters).
